key_insight: A unified analytical model can both diagnose where photoelectrochemical cells lose energy and translate those losses into rational design rules for improving efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The framework gives engineers a practical way to compare BIJ and SEJ photoelectrodes, fit experimental IV curves, and target fixes such as better junction matching, nanostructuring, or co-catalysts.
method: Builds a physically consistent loss model for light absorption, transport, recombination, and interfacial charge transfer.
Generates current-voltage curves, efficiency maps, and Sankey energy-flow diagrams under ideal and real conditions.
Fits experimental IV data to decompose losses quantitatively and identify bottlenecks in specific devices.
evidence_signal: The abstract says the model is validated against literature results across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries, covering multiple material classes.
watch_item: The approach depends on fitting and model assumptions, so accuracy may degrade if device physics or interfacial parameters are not well captured.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
